snippet.title: MAX - Stupid in Love (Live Performance) | Vevo
snippet.description:
MAX - Stupid in Love. An exclusive performance for Vevo. 

Evolution is a key ingredient to pop longevity, and it’s been fun watching MAX continue to add strands to his artistic DNA. The sharp singer made a huge splash in 2016 with “Lights Down Low,” a mid tempo ballad - notably sung entirely by himself - that racked up hundreds of millions of streams. But even on his debut album, ‘Hell’s Kitchen Angel,’ the New York native’s yen for collaboration was made apparent by features from Lil Uzi Vert and Hoodie Allen. Working with others is a gateway to new processes, perspectives, and worldviews, of course, and for MAX it’s been the key to staying fresh. 2020 saw the arrival of two projects: one was ’Neon From Now On’ released by Party Pupils, his house music side project with producer/DJ pal Ryan Siegler. The other was the pristinely-produced ‘Colour Vision.’ Here’s an incomplete list of artists credited on that record: the meme-rapper bbno$, indie pop darling Quinn XCX, rapper Joey Bada$$, and pop star Kim Petras. Diverse as can be. And that’s not to mention BTS member SUGA, whose “Blueberry Eyes” contribution was a huge crossover K-Pop hit. We've been keen to point our cameras at MAX over the last few years, in fact these performances of tracks from his new ‘LOVE IN STEREO’ album is his third session with Vevo. Fans seem to dig the stripped down vibe he typically brings, wherein the volume shifts down and the emphasis on his silky vocals and emotional lyrics ramps up. This third LP is already doing big numbers, by the way. “IT’S YOU,” which on the album features fellow Vevo fave keshi, has already crossed the 100 million stream rubicon on Spotify. The title track is hot too. Tap into these smooth jams, then take it to the MAX with the album.

snippet.title: MAX, Ali Gatie - Butterflies (Live Performance) | Vevo
snippet.description:
MAX ft. Ali Gatie - Butterflies. An exclusive live performance for Vevo.

If you peel back the tasty layers of pop production on most any MAX song, you’ll find a tender love song at the core. Check, for instance, the multiplatinum singer’s sophomore album, ‘Colour Vision.’ It’s packed with classic MAX configurations made to bust both your car speakers and your heart. Putting aside the bells and whistles is what artists typically do at the Vevo studio, and it gave the New Yorker a chance to really dig in deep on those emotions. Since his 2016 debut album, ‘Hell’s Kitchen Angel,’ (we’ll never forget the mohawk) MAX has emphasized non-traditional collaborations — lest we forget, Lil Uzi Vert made an appearance on that record. BTS superstar Suga, alt-rapper bbno$, cult faves Chromeo, and Quinn XCII all put their imprint on ‘Colour Vision.’ So it was no surprise that MAX made it a point to have Canadian crooner Ali Gatie with him to perform their new single “Butterflies.” Clearly in the romance mood that day, MAX also dove into a version of Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You.” Share both with your sweetheart, they’ll thank you for it.

MAX - Stupid in Love (Live Performance) | Vevo
snippet.description:
MAX - Stupid in Love. An exclusive performance for Vevo. 

Evolution is a key ingredient to pop longevity, and it’s been fun watching MAX continue to add strands to his artistic DNA. The sharp singer made a huge splash in 2016 with “Lights Down Low,” a mid tempo ballad - notably sung entirely by himself - that racked up hundreds of millions of streams. But even on his debut album, ‘Hell’s Kitchen Angel,’ the New York native’s yen for collaboration was made apparent by features from Lil Uzi Vert and Hoodie Allen. Working with others is a gateway to new processes, perspectives, and worldviews, of course, and for MAX it’s been the key to staying fresh. 2020 saw the arrival of two projects: one was ’Neon From Now On’ released by Party Pupils, his house music side project with producer/DJ pal Ryan Siegler. The other was the pristinely-produced ‘Colour Vision.’ Here’s an incomplete list of artists credited on that record: the meme-rapper bbno$, indie pop darling Quinn XCX, rapper Joey Bada$$, and pop star Kim Petras. Diverse as can be. And that’s not to mention BTS member SUGA, whose “Blueberry Eyes” contribution was a huge crossover K-Pop hit. We've been keen to point our cameras at MAX over the last few years, in fact these performances of tracks from his new ‘LOVE IN STEREO’ album is his third session with Vevo. Fans seem to dig the stripped down vibe he typically brings, wherein the volume shifts down and the emphasis on his silky vocals and emotional lyrics ramps up. This third LP is already doing big numbers, by the way. “IT’S YOU,” which on the album features fellow Vevo fave keshi, has already crossed the 100 million stream rubicon on Spotify. The title track is hot too. Tap into these smooth jams, then take it to the MAX with the album.

snippet.title: MAX, Ali Gatie - Butterflies (Live Performance) | Vevo
snippet.description:
MAX ft. Ali Gatie - Butterflies. An exclusive live performance for Vevo.

If you peel back the tasty layers of pop production on most any MAX song, you’ll find a tender love song at the core. Check, for instance, the multiplatinum singer’s sophomore album, ‘Colour Vision.’ It’s packed with classic MAX configurations made to bust both your car speakers and your heart. Putting aside the bells and whistles is what artists typically do at the Vevo studio, and it gave the New Yorker a chance to really dig in deep on those emotions. Since his 2016 debut album, ‘Hell’s Kitchen Angel,’ (we’ll never forget the mohawk) MAX has emphasized non-traditional collaborations — lest we forget, Lil Uzi Vert made an appearance on that record. BTS superstar Suga, alt-rapper bbno$, cult faves Chromeo, and Quinn XCII all put their imprint on ‘Colour Vision.’ So it was no surprise that MAX made it a point to have Canadian crooner Ali Gatie with him to perform their new single “Butterflies.” Clearly in the romance mood that day, MAX also dove into a version of Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You.” Share both with your sweetheart, they’ll thank you for it.

MAX – “Acid Dreams” (Studio Performance)

Once you've got the knack for cranking out earworms, you can really turn some heads around. Max Schneider has that knack, and ever since "Lights Down Low" trickled out into the world in 2016 under the single moniker MAX, he's been on a roll. If you'd been paying close attention, you probably know that Schneider had a couple of earlier releases back at the start of the decade. There he revealed his bedrock skills, but these days, with 'Hell's Kitchen Angel' behind him and an endless string of collabs that stretches from Hoody Allen to Noah Cyrus to Illenium to gnash, he's a true pop pro firing on all cylinders. He came into roll through "Acid Dreams" and version of "Love Me Less" that features Quinn XCII. Both are pretty addictive.

MAX ft. Quinn XCII – “Love Me Less” (Studio Performance)

Once you've got the knack for cranking out earworms, you can really turn some heads around. Max Schneider has that knack, and ever since "Lights Down Low" trickled out into the world in 2016 under the single moniker MAX, he's been on a roll. If you'd been paying close attention, you probably know that Schneider had a couple of earlier releases back at the start of the decade. There he revealed his bedrock skills, but these days, after his 'Hell's Kitchen Angel' behind him and an endless string of collabs that stretches from Hoody Allen to Noah Cyrus to Illenium to gnash, he's a true pop pro and firing on all cylinders. Speaking of collabs, this live performance of "Love Me Less" features Quinn XCII. It, too, is pretty addictive.
